noMetricsServer: metrics-server is not installed or not answering: real CPU and memory usage cannot be measured. Requested (requests) and allocatable resources are still shown, as they come from the configuration. Install metrics-server in the cluster to enable real usage.
noMetricsServerShort: Per-Pod usage not available: metrics-server is not installed.
noDataPoints: No data in the selected range.
prometheusNotConfigured: History and network traffic require Prometheus, which is not configured.
prometheusError: Prometheus is configured but not answering: {{error}}
partial: Partial data: some resources cannot be read with the permissions of the Scarlet Kubernetes account ({{kinds}}).
requestsExplain: Requests are the resources Pods reserve: Kubernetes uses them to decide which node runs them. When the requests on a node reach 100% new Pods stay Pending even if real usage is low. Limits are the maximum a container can use: above the memory limit the container is killed (OOMKilled), above the CPU limit it is throttled.
nearLimit: Close to the memory limit: OOMKilled risk

cpu.title: CPU
cpu.subtitle: CPU usage of the cluster, nodes and Pods, compared with requested and available resources.

memory.title: Memory
memory.subtitle: Memory usage of the cluster, nodes and Pods, compared with requests and limits.

storage.title: Storage
storage.subtitle: Persistent volumes of the cluster: space requests (PVC), capacity per storage class and usage.
storage.usageNeedsPrometheus: The used space percentage of volumes requires Prometheus with the kubelet_volume_stats metrics. Without Prometheus only capacity and status are shown.

health.title: Health
health.subtitle: Status of the components the application depends on. Optional components never make the system Unhealthy.

overallText.degraded: The application works but some components are missing, disabled or have non-blocking problems.
overallText.unhealthy: One or more essential components do not work: some features are unavailable.

describe.database: The SQLite database with users, audit and settings.
describe.kubernetes: Connection to the cluster API server.
describe.podman: Connection to the Podman API on this host.
describe.storage: Free space in the Scarlet data directory.
describe.metrics_server: Provides real CPU and memory usage.
describe.prometheus: Provides history, network and volume usage.
describe.backup: Age of the last successful Scarlet backup.

msg.kubernetes_unavailable: Cannot verify: Kubernetes is not connected
msg.old: The last backup is older than 2 days

problem.no_tls: HTTPS not active (neither TLS nor reverse proxy)
problem.plain_http_exposed: Plain HTTP exposed on all interfaces

ha.title: High availability
ha.subtitle: How well applications survive the loss of a Pod or a node: replicas, spread over nodes, probes, resources and disruption protection.

replica.title: Replica
replica.text: An identical copy of the application. With several replicas, if one stops the others keep serving users.

rollingUpdate.title: Rolling update
rollingUpdate.text: Progressive update: new versions replace old ones a few at a time, without stopping the service.

rollback.title: Rollback
rollback.text: Going back to the previous version if an update causes problems.

readiness.title: Readiness probe
readiness.text: Check telling Kubernetes when a Pod is ready to receive traffic. Without it, traffic can reach an application that has not started yet.

liveness.title: Liveness probe
liveness.text: Check that detects a stuck application and restarts it automatically.

request.title: Resource request
request.text: Resources reserved for the Pod: they ensure the chosen node has enough room.

limit.title: Resource limit
limit.text: Maximum resources usable: protects other Pods from an application consuming too much.

disruption.title: Pod disruption
disruption.text: A PodDisruptionBudget limits how many replicas can be stopped together during maintenance (e.g. node drain).

ha.resilientHint: several replicas on several nodes, all ready
ha.fewNodes: The cluster has fewer than 2 ready nodes: losing a node interrupts all applications.

sentence.stopped: Scaled to zero: the application is stopped.
sentence.single: It has a single replica: if the Pod stops the service is interrupted until Kubernetes starts another one.
sentence.sameNode: It has {{count}} replicas but all on the same node: if the node stops the service is interrupted.
sentence.multi: This application has {{count}} replicas on {{nodes}} nodes. If a Pod is lost, Kubernetes can automatically create another one.

flagHelp.single_replica: Raise replicas to at least 2 (Operations → Scale).
flagHelp.same_node: All replicas run on one node: consider a topologySpreadConstraint or anti-affinity.
flagHelp.no_pdb: Without a PodDisruptionBudget a drain can stop all replicas at once.
flagHelp.no_readiness: Traffic can reach Pods that are not ready yet during starts and updates.
flagHelp.no_liveness: A stuck application is not restarted automatically.
flagHelp.no_requests: Without requests the scheduler guarantees no resources and the Pod is the first to be evicted.
flagHelp.no_memory_limit: Without a memory limit a container can consume the node's memory.

events.title: Events
events.subtitle: What Kubernetes recently did or reported. Warnings are shown first.
events.retentionNote: Kubernetes keeps events for a limited time (1 hour by default): history needs an external logging system.

logs.title: Logs
logs.subtitle: Container logs of Kubernetes Pods: last lines, previous run and live streaming.
logs.noPermission: Your role does not allow reading logs (permission logs.read).
logs.filterPending: Filter to apply: "{{filter}}". Choose namespace and Pod.
